summary: Evaluate a clipped power-law envelope on a normalized two-dimensional flux grid, with optional explicit reference fluxes and exponent.

capability: Evaluate a clipped power-law envelope on a normalized two-dimensional flux grid, with optional explicit reference fluxes and exponent.
operation: evaluate the clipped Frank-Egedal radial envelope
(psi, psi_axis=None, psi_edge=None, alpha=1.0) -> radial envelope array with the shape of psi
discovery.model: Source-defined radial multiplier for a Frank-Egedal pressure construction; it does not compute a pressure or equilibrium
discovery.geometry: Caller-supplied two-dimensional axisymmetric flux samples; no radial coordinate or magnetic geometry is reconstructed
discovery.boundary: The normalized coordinate is clipped to [0,1], so the envelope is constant outside the interval. Reversing psi_axis and psi_edge reverses its orientation. No spatial boundary condition is solved.

identity.relation: Flux grid and radial profile controls to a dimensionless pressure-source envelope
identity.direction: (psi, psi_axis=None, psi_edge=None, alpha=1.0) -> radial envelope array with the shape of psi
identity.definition: Let u=clip((psi-psi_axis)/(psi_edge-psi_axis),0,1). Return [clip(1-u,0,infinity)]^alpha elementwise. psi_axis defaults to min(psi), psi_edge to max(psi), and alpha to 1.0. Both signs of the finite nonzero flux interval are accepted; alpha=0 makes the entire clipped grid equal one, including the outer endpoint, by NumPy's zero-power convention.
identity.model: Source-defined radial multiplier for a Frank-Egedal pressure construction; it does not compute a pressure or equilibrium
identity.geometry: Caller-supplied two-dimensional axisymmetric flux samples; no radial coordinate or magnetic geometry is reconstructed
identity.coordinates: The array is indexed [Z,R] by the declared contract. psi, psi_axis and psi_edge must share one caller-selected flux convention; the historical descriptor labels psi in Wb, but the callable does not enforce or convert that convention.
identity.boundary: The normalized coordinate is clipped to [0,1], so the envelope is constant outside the interval. Reversing psi_axis and psi_edge reverses its orientation. No spatial boundary condition is solved.
assumptions: The two reference fluxes denote distinct levels in the same units and normalization as psi.
The exponent is finite and nonnegative; this source-defined envelope alone makes no statement about the physical pressure profile or its normalization.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.description: Axisymmetric flux grid whose elements are normalized between two reference levels.
inputs.units: same flux unit as psi_axis and psi_edge; historical source label Wb
inputs.constraints: np.asarray(..., dtype=float) must produce a finite two-dimensional nonempty array.

inputs.name: psi_axis
inputs.description: Flux at the profile axis; None selects the grid minimum.
inputs.constraints: Finite after float conversion when supplied.

inputs.name: psi_edge
inputs.description: Flux at the profile edge; None selects the grid maximum.
inputs.constraints: Finite after float conversion when supplied; distinct from psi_axis by at least 1e-30 in absolute value.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: Power-law exponent for the clipped envelope.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative after float conversion.

outputs.name: radial_envelope
outputs.description: Direct array return of the clipped source-order radial multiplier, not a key in a result mapping.
outputs.constraints: For successful finite arithmetic, values lie in [0,1]. An alpha of zero returns ones, even at u=1; there is no post-computation finite-output validation.

preconditions: psi is a finite nonempty 2-D grid, and explicit reference/exponent values are finite scalar-convertible values.
The selected axis and edge fluxes define a finite nonzero interval at least 1e-30 in absolute size.
supported: Forward and reverse flux orientations and nonnegative power-law exponents on a clipped normalized interval.
Caller-supplied reference fluxes or grid extrema as defaults.
excluded: Inferring a physically correct axis, edge, flux unit or pressure normalization from the grid.
A full Frank-Egedal closure, magnetic-field calculation, coordinate conversion or extrapolation beyond the clipped interval.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for a nonfinite, empty or non-2-D psi grid; nonfinite reference/exponent values; negative exponent; or a reference interval with abs(psi_edge-psi_axis)<1e-30. Float-conversion errors may propagate as ValueError or TypeError.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Array allocation or arithmetic errors can propagate. No general finite-output check follows the power evaluation, and extreme finite values may encounter floating-point warnings or nonfinite intermediate arithmetic.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; evaluation is elementwise without iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial array is returned on a raised exception. A successful call returns only the envelope array.

example.description: Apply a quadratic envelope on a grid with values both inside and outside the chosen flux interval.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.mirror import evaluate_frank_egedal_radial_envelope
psi = np.array([[-1.0, 0.0, 0.5], [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]])
r = evaluate_frank_egedal_radial_envelope(
    psi, psi_axis=0.0, psi_edge=1.0, alpha=2.0
)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r, [[1.0, 1.0, 0.25], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
assert r.shape == psi.shape
example.expected: Observed PASS: The clipped quadratic envelope is [[1, 1, 0.25], [0, 0, 0]] and retains the input grid shape.

scope: Direct two-row closed-form examples for quadratic and linear exponents, clipped endpoints and reverse flux orientation.
Affine flux relabeling, default reference extrema, zero exponent, input ownership and selected invalid-grid/reference cases.

known_limitations: Reference flux levels and flux convention are supplied or inferred from grid extrema, not physically identified by this function.
The historical Wb label and other SciRel Wb/rad flux conventions have no automatic conversion; the tested coupling requires axis/edge references to share the current psi coordinate.
A zero exponent yields one even at the clipped edge; finite extrema can still trigger extreme arithmetic without a post-computation check.
The independent analytic comparison does not replace an external experimental reference.
